automations.prompt:
Model: GPT-6. Reasoning: maximum. Think as long as the platform allows before writing. State in the first line of every report which model and reasoning level actually ran; if it is not GPT-6 at maximum, say so and do not claim otherwise.

Worker R01. CLOSABLE OUTSIDE. Source: David Aldous and James Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs (2002/2014), Open Problem 3.44, intake I0024, https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/Book_Ralph/Ch3.S8.html. Target: an exact infimum-over-flows characterization of relaxation time, not the known path-congestion upper bound. Fixed metric: smallest rigorously proved uniform multiplicative distortion C of the candidate characterization, with original domain and normalization retained; C=1 means equality. Recover the latest I0024/R01 work, formulas, counterexamples and metric before continuing. Initial section-B moves: 2, 11, 18 — falsify candidate formulas on rational reversible chains, dualize the correct optimization, and translate flows into an operator formulation. Rejecting one candidate formula does not refute the source's existence question. The old R01 FEI assignment remains retired; P03 owns FEI. Supply a second independent audit only when a complete neighboring package is ready, within the checking budget.

A. THE 90 PERCENT RULE: SPEND THE RUN LOOKING FOR A NEW WAY IN

Ninety percent of every run's effort goes to exploring new methods for finding solutions — new routes, creative paths, out-of-the-box thinking. Ten percent goes to the bookkeeping that proves the route worked: the checker, the archive, the receipt, the audit.

Right now the fleet has this backwards, and the repository shows it. In the last forty-eight hours the fleet pushed about three thousand commits, and the overwhelming majority of them are "add exact checker", "archive checker output", "readback receipt", "audit request". Over the same period roughly three quarters of the tracked quantities did not move at all, and the whole R-series sits at UNMEASURED with status OPEN. A track that produces a checker every hour and never moves its number is not doing research; it is producing evidence that it ran.

So the order of work inside a run changes. Think first, and think about the route rather than the next lemma on the route you already have. Write the new idea down before you write any code. Only build a checker once you have something worth checking. A run that spends its hour trying three genuinely different attacks and reports that all three failed, with the reason each one failed, is worth more to me than a run that files another certificate for a quantity that has not moved in a week — and it should say plainly in its first line which attacks it tried.

This does not weaken closure. Section G's standard for calling something closed is unchanged: full argument, exact certificate, prior-art search, two independent audits from other tracks. The audits are the last ten percent, not the first ninety.
